content.title:
Texas Monthly on Instagram: "Tacos and taquerias have long held political significance in the United States. Remember the 2016 election-season “threat” from a Donald Trump surrogate that the U.S. could turn into a country with taco trucks on every corner? The latest reminder is the pithy acronym coined by Financial Times columnist Robert Armstrong, TACO—“Trump Always Chickens Out”—referring to Trump’s trade threats. Tacos themselves aren’t immune to economic upheaval, as key ingredients grown in Mexico and imported to the U.S., such as limes, tomatoes, and avocados, are set to become more expensive soon due to tariffs.

It’s a reminder that Mexico and Mexicans have contributed much to the country and are foundationally important to the United States. “To truly honor tacos means honoring the people behind them,” says Joseph Gomez, owner of Austin’s Sana Sana Taqueria and a Rio Grande Valley native.

📸: José R. Ralat"
